text:
IncidentBot: PAGER: [sev-2] eu-west serving cluster — large number of container restarts + CUDA OOMs observed. Alert: autoscaler thrash detected (scale-up -> immediate scale-down) causing crashloops. Pager: monica_oncall, sara_sre

monica_oncall: Confirming. Saw the alert spike at 14:03 UTC. Looking at grafana now.

sara_sre: +1 I'm on metrics. CPU ok but GPU memory used skyrockets before OOMs, then pods restart. Autoscaler events show 20 -> 60 -> 18 nodes in ~8m.

ash_infra: Replaying autoscaler logs: stabilization window is 60s, but scale-down cooldown set low, combined with bursty queue seems to cause oscillation. Also seeing kubelet evictions on some nodes right before restarts.

monica_oncall: Copy. Pulling a pod log.

monica_oncall: ```
logs (runtime-pod-5f8c):
2026-03-15T14:04:12Z runtime: allocate tensors size=6.2Gi
2026-03-15T14:04:13Z runtime: nvml: GPU 0: memory high
2026-03-15T14:04:13Z runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T14:04:13Z runtime: panic: oom when allocating KV cache

kubernetes: container exited with code 137
```

ash_infra: Node-level logs show kernel OOM killer invoked on worker-3 right before container exit.

ryan_next_oncall: Are we seeing a specific model causing this?

monica_oncall: Looking at request traces: sudden increase in long-context chat requests (seq len > 8k) to model redwood-llm-large-v2 on this pool. Most affected pods running that model variant.

liz_cs: Customer impact: CS triage flagged 6 customers with elevated 504s and token timeouts in last 15m. Opening a ticket thread to notify impacted customers now.

monica_oncall: Mitigations I'm executing now: 1) Pause autoscaler scale-down (bump cool-down) 2) Cordon a few flaky nodes 3) Roll back recent runtime image patch (deployed 13:58) to previous stable 2026-03-15_1350

deploy-bot: deployment rollback initiated: runtime-service -> rollback to tag v1.8.9 by monica_oncall (CI-ID 6723). ETA ~2m.

ash_infra: I'm increasing node pool target by +20 GPUs to reduce immediate scheduling pressure.

monica_oncall: Also flipping an emergency routing rule: route long-context requests to fallback model redwood-llm-medium-v1 (slower but lower memory). Doing a canary 10% -> 100% if stable.

sara_sre: Watchlist: rate of container restarts stopped climbing after rollback started. Pod restart rate down from 34/min to 6/min in last 2m.

ryan_next_oncall: Good. I'm taking over the pager (handoff). Monica — can you summarize what you've done and outstanding action items?

monica_oncall: Handoff summary: - Paused scale-down and increased cooldown to 10m - Rolled back runtime image to v1.8.9 - Cordoned worker-2/3/7 (flaky) - Increased pool target +20 GPUs - Emergency routing to fallback model enabled (10% canary) - Notified CS to contact impacted customers

monica_oncall: Outstanding: 1) Validate that rollback fully mitigates OOMs 2) Monitor autoscaler behavior and re-enable controlled scaling (with damping) 3) Run heap/cuda mem diagnostics on cordoned nodes 4) Decide whether to drain and replace 3 nodes

ryan_next_oncall: Thanks. I'll take lead. First steps: keep rollback live for 10m, bump canary to 50% if OOMs not reappearing, start controlled drain for worker-3.

ash_infra: Starting diagnostics: `ssh node-worker-3 -- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` — pushing results in 30s.

deploy-bot: rollback complete: runtime-service -> v1.8.9 rolled back in 1m35s. All new pods being scheduled.

monica_oncall: Observability: latency p50 back to baseline, p95 still elevated. Error rate for redwood-llm-large-v2 down 70%.

ash_infra: Diagnostics: worker-3 dmesg shows repeated OOM killer invocations for processes named runtime, nv_peer_mem messages noisy. nvidia-smi shows GPU memory fragmentation high (80-95%).

sara_sre: Autoscaler events: we still see a couple of scale-downs triggered because metrics (cpu) drop quickly after the brief spikes. Need a metric that is GPU memory pressure-aware.

ryan_next_oncall: Action: (1) Add a temporary autoscale policy to throttle scale-downs based on pending pod GPU requests and active GPU memory pressure metric. (2) Increase stabilization window to 600s. (3) Schedule replace for worker-3 if diagnostics show persistent GPU driver instability.

liz_cs: CS update: initial customer notifications sent for 6 customers with root-cause summary and ETA for follow-up. Will escalate any paid support pings.

monica_oncall: Noted: Also found a small config change in runtime v1.9.0 that increases KV cache prefetch size under high-concurrency — likely amplified memory use. That change was in the 13:58 release we rolled back.

ryan_next_oncall: Thanks. Next checks: after 10m, if no significant OOMs and restart rate stays low, we gradually re-enable controlled scale-down. If restarts climb, begin full draining of cordoned nodes and failover traffic to other pools/regions.

ash_infra: I'm opening infra ticket INF-2026-345 to track node replacements and driver rollout.

sara_sre: Logging note for postmortem: autoscaler cooldowns + aggressive prefetching in v1.9.0 caused memory amplification for long-context workloads -> oscillation. We'll assign action items.

monica_oncall: I'll join the postmortem. For now, monitoring looks stable. Handing off active paging to ryan_next_oncall.

ryan_next_oncall: Taking over. I'll keep the thread updated every 5m while we stabilize. If we see regression, I'll page infra and oncall core.

liz_cs: Thanks team — updating customer thread with post-rollback status and action plan.

IncidentBot: NOTE: On-call handoff recorded: monica_oncall -> ryan_next_oncall at 14:09 UTC.

ryan_next_oncall: 14:14 update: pod restart rate steady at 2/min, no new CUDA OOMs in last 6m, canary bumped to 40%. Continuing to monitor.

sara_sre: tagging for postmortem owners: monica_oncall (eng-runtime), ash_infra (infra), sara_sre (sre), liz_cs (cs).

ryan_next_oncall: If all good at 14:35 UTC, I'll close the pager and open incident review doc with timeline and remediation tasks.

monica_oncall: Thanks all — leaving oncall notes in the runbook. :white_check_mark:
